originalTitle: Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say
title: A Sad Story in Sudan: Wishing for Peace
content:
Hello, Young Friends!

Hello, my wonderful friends across Africa and beyond! It's your friendly news reporter here. Today, I have some news to share with you from a country called Sudan. It's a bit of a sad story, but it's important for us to understand what's happening and why we always hope for peace and kindness in our world. Sometimes, grown-ups have big problems, and we need to talk about them simply.

What Happened in Sudan?

In a place far away, in Sudan, something very sad happened. There was fighting, and some flying robots called drones were used. These drones hit a truck that was carrying people. Where were these people going? They were going to a funeral. A funeral is a very special and sad time when people gather to remember someone they loved who has passed away. They go to say goodbye and comfort each other. Imagine being sad and then something else bad happens. It's very, very hard.

More Sad News

These drones also hit a place called a market. Do you know what a market is? It's a busy place where people go to buy and sell things. Like yummy fruits, colorful clothes, or even fuel for cars and machines. In this market, people were selling fuel. The army in Sudan thought that this market was giving fuel to another group of people they were fighting with. So, they targeted the market too.

So Many People Hurt

Because of these sad events, many, many people were hurt. And sadly, over 300 people lost their lives. That's a very big number, like many, many children in your school. These were fathers, mothers, brothers, sisters, friends, and neighbors. When something like this happens, it makes everyone very, very sad and scared. We always wish for everyone to be safe and sound.

Where is Sudan?

Sudan is a very big country in Africa. It's in the part of Africa that has a lot of sand and a big river called the Nile. It's full of kind people and beautiful places. It's a country with a long history and amazing stories. It's important to remember that even when sad things happen in a place, the people there are still good and strong. **Did you know?** Sudan is one of the largest countries in Africa! It has famous pyramids, just like Egypt, but not as many tourists know about them yet.

What are Drones?

Imagine a flying toy airplane, but much bigger and stronger. That's a bit like a drone! Drones are special flying machines that can fly without a pilot sitting inside. They can be controlled from far away by people using computers. Sometimes, drones are used for good things, like taking amazing pictures from high up, or even delivering medicines to faraway places that are hard to reach by car. **Did you know?** Drones are also used to help farmers check on their crops or to see if there are wildfires starting in forests! They can do many helpful jobs.

Why Does Fighting Happen?

Sometimes, grown-ups in a country have very big disagreements. When they can't talk and agree on things, they might start fighting. This is called a 'conflict' or a 'war'. In Sudan, there are two main groups who are fighting right now: the 'Sudan Army' (who are like the official soldiers of the country) and another group called the 'Rapid Support Forces' (or RSF). They are fighting over who gets to lead the country and how things should be done. It's a very complicated problem, and sadly, it's the ordinary people who get hurt the most. **Did you know?** When people fight, it often makes everyone in the country sad and makes it hard to go to school or get food. That's why peace is so important!

What is a Funeral?

Let's talk a bit more about funerals. When someone we love passes away, it's a very difficult time. A funeral is a ceremony where family and friends come together. They might pray, share stories about the person they loved, and remember them. It's a time to feel sad together and also to support each other. It's a very peaceful and personal time for families. **Did you know?** Different cultures and religions around the world have unique and special ways to say goodbye to loved ones, but they all share the common idea of remembering and honoring someone.

What is a Market?

A market is a very lively and often noisy place! It’s where people gather to buy and sell all sorts of things. You can find fresh vegetables, colourful fabrics, handmade crafts, and many other goods. In African countries, markets are often at the heart of the community. They are places where friends meet, news is shared, and people earn their living. To hit a market means to hurt many, many people at once. **Did you know?** Some markets in Africa are so big, they stretch for many kilometers and are open every single day!

Wishing for Peace and Kindness

This sad news from Sudan reminds us how important it is for everyone to live in peace. When there is fighting, people get hurt, and many good things stop happening, like children going to school or families being together. We should always wish for peace, for leaders to talk instead of fight, and for everyone to be kind to each other. Even though we are far away, we can send our good thoughts and hopes for peace to the people of Sudan. Let's remember to be kind and helpful to everyone around us, every single day.
summary: A sad incident in Sudan saw drones hit people attending a funeral and a market, tragically killing over 300 people, amidst ongoing conflict between the army and another group.
whyMatters: This is important because it shows how fighting between grown-ups can hurt many innocent people, making us all wish for peace, safety, and kindness in every country.

originalTitle: Nigeria confirms Ebola case linked to East Africa
title: News From Mama Koko: Keeping Safe in Nigeria!
content:
Hello, my wonderful friends all across Africa! It's Mama Koko, your friendly news reporter, here to share something important with you. We always want to learn new things and stay safe, right? That's why I'm here to talk about some news from a country called Nigeria.

A Special Lady in Nigeria

There is a lady who is not feeling very well in Nigeria. She is in a special place, a hospital in a big city called Abuja. Doctors and nurses are taking very good care of her. They are helping her to get better.

What is Ebola?

Now, this lady has something called Ebola. Have you heard of it? It's a kind of sickness. Sometimes, tiny, tiny germs can make people sick. Ebola is one of those sicknesses. But don't worry, it's not like a common cold that spreads very easily. **Did you know?** Ebola is named after a river in Africa! It was first found near the Ebola River a long, long time ago. Ebola germs don't fly in the air like dust. They spread if someone touches a very sick person's blood or other body liquids. That's why doctors and nurses wear special clothes to protect themselves.

Staying Safe in Hospital

This lady is in a special room in the hospital. It's called an "isolation room." Imagine a room where you can stay all by yourself. This is like that, but it's to keep germs from spreading to other people. It's a very clever way to make sure everyone else stays healthy. The doctors and nurses are super brave and kind. They are working hard to help the lady feel better. They give her medicine and make sure she is comfortable. This is called "medical care."

From Far Away?

The doctors think this sickness might be "linked to East Africa." What does that mean? Well, sometimes people travel from one country to another. Or maybe this sickness is similar to one that was seen in another part of Africa, far away from Nigeria. Africa is a very big continent with many beautiful countries! It just means doctors are trying to understand everything so they can help everyone stay safe. It's like solving a puzzle!

How We Keep Ourselves Safe

Mama Koko wants you to remember some very important things. These things help us stay safe from *all* kinds of germs, not just Ebola! * **Wash Your Hands!** This is super important! Use soap and clean water. Sing your favorite song while you wash, for at least 20 seconds. Wash your hands before you eat, after you use the toilet, and after you play outside. **Did you know?** Washing your hands with soap and water is one of the best ways to stop germs from spreading! It's like having tiny superheroes on your hands, washing away the bad guys! * **Don't Touch Your Face:** Try not to touch your eyes, nose, or mouth with unwashed hands. Germs love to sneak into our bodies through these places. * **Tell a Grown-Up:** If you ever feel sick, or if someone you know is sick, tell a grown-up right away. Tell your mum, dad, grandma, grandpa, or your teacher. They will know what to do. It's brave to tell an adult! * **Stay Home When Sick:** If you are not feeling well, it's best to stay home from school or playing with friends. This helps you get better faster and stops germs from spreading to your friends.

What is Nigeria Doing?

Nigeria is a big and strong country. The doctors and nurses there are very smart. The government (that's the people who help run the country) is also working hard. They are making sure the lady gets the best help. They are also checking to make sure no one else gets sick. They want to keep everyone in Nigeria healthy and happy. **Did you know?** Nigeria is home to many different kinds of people and has amazing culture, music, and food! It's one of the biggest countries in Africa!

Why This Matters to Us

This news matters because it reminds us that we are all part of one big family in Africa. When something happens in one country, we learn from it and support each other. It shows us that doctors and nurses are heroes who work very hard to keep us well. It also teaches us how important it is to be clean and careful, not just for ourselves, but for our whole community. By washing our hands and telling adults when we are sick, we are helping everyone around us stay healthy too. We are all "health helpers"!

Mama Koko Says "Stay Strong!"

So, my dear friends, remember to be kind, be clean, and be brave! There are amazing people working hard to keep everyone safe. We learn, we grow, and we stay strong together. Keep washing those hands, tell your grown-ups if you don't feel well, and always remember to share a smile. That's all for today from Mama Koko, your friendly news reporter for Africa! See you next time!
summary: A lady in Nigeria is being cared for by doctors for a sickness called Ebola, reminding us all to stay clean and tell grown-ups if we feel unwell.
whyMatters: This is important because it teaches us about staying healthy and safe, and how doctors work hard to help people, showing we can all be strong together in Africa.
